newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian opposition rejects government olive branch.
newsitem.headline: Italian opposition rejects government olive branch.

text.p: Italy's centre-right opposition on Tuesday rejected a government move to resolve a bitter stand-off over the 1997 budget.

Silvio Berlusconi's Freedom Alliance said on Monday it would not vote on the budget as part of a protest at government plans to take special powers which would allow it to dictate policy on key budgetary areas without having to refer back to parliament.

Its main objection centred on a planned reform of the fiscal system, with the government only providing a bare outline of the proposed measures. In a bid to defuse the row, Italian Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco earlier on Tuesday gave more details.

But the Freedom Alliance said they were being offered too little too late. "The government wants parliament to decide in the space of two days a fiscal reform which is destined to condition the future of the country for many years to come," the statement said.
It added that the fiscal proposals should be stripped from the budget and examined separately next year.
"The Alliance wants parliament to discuss the fiscal reform...and establish explicitly who pays and how much they pay," the statemenet added.

The government can still get the budget through parliament without the presence of the opposition, but the Alliance's refusal to cooperate challenges the legitimacy of the final vote on the package. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
